intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Wander through centuries of Bohemian history with stunning panoramic views over the red-roofed city below.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. Enjoy indoor and outdoor pools fed by natural hot springs, a deeply rooted Hungarian cultural tradition dating back to Ottoman rule.

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Walking Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided walking tour through the medieval Old Town Square, witnessing the famous 15th-century Astronomical Clock chime on the hour, exploring Gothic churches, Baroque palaces, and hearing stories of Kafka, alchemists, and the Holy Roman Empire.

experiences.name: Budapest Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Sail along the Danube at dusk and witness the illuminated UNESCO-listed panorama of the Hungarian Parliament, Buda Castle, and the Chain Bridge. An unforgettable way to appreciate Budapest's architectural grandeur and understand why it's called the 'Pearl of the Danube.'
experiences.location: Vigadó Square Pier, Pest Embankment, Budapest

experiences.name: Czech & Hungarian Street Food & Market Crawl
experiences.description: Explore Prague's Manifesto Market and Budapest's Great Market Hall to taste local delicacies including trdelník, svíčková, lángos, and chimney cake. A self-guided culinary journey through both cities' food heritage, blending Austro-Hungarian flavors with modern street food culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take the Airport Express Bus (Line AE) to Dejvická metro station, then Metro Line A to Malostranská or Hradčanská stop (~50 CZK total, ~45 min). Check into your Hradčany boutique stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed orientation walk around Hradčany Square (Hradčanské náměstí). Admire the Archbishop's Palace and Schwarzenberg Palace exteriors for free. Stroll along Loretánská Street to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Walk downhill through Nerudova Street — one of Prague's most picturesque cobblestone lanes — toward Malá Strana (Lesser Town). Cross the iconic Charles Bridge at dusk for stunning views of Prague Castle lit up behind you. Enjoy the atmospheric lantern-lit bridge and street musicians.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap bite near the airport or at a bakery (pekárna) near your hotel — try a fresh trdelník or open-faced chlebíčky sandwich for 40–60 CZK.
meals.dinner: Lokál Malá Strana (Míšeňská 12) — a beloved Czech pub serving affordable traditional food. Try svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings for ~180–220 CZK. Pilsner Urquell on tap ~55 CZK.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Keep the evening short and save energy for full days ahead. Buy a 3-day Prague public transport pass (~330 CZK) at the airport or metro station for great savings.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex visit — start early to beat crowds. Enter via the castle gates (free to walk the courtyards). Purchase the shorter Circuit B ticket (~250 CZK) covering St. Vitus Cathedral, Old Royal Palace, and St. George's Basilica. Spend 2–3 hours exploring. The Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička) with its colorful tiny houses is included and unmissable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to Malá Strana and visit the Baroque Wallenstein Garden (free entry) — a hidden gem with peacocks and classical statues. Then head to Kampa Island via the 'Devil's Stream' canal — a tranquil park area perfect for a picnic lunch. Browse the outdoor John Lennon Wall (free) covered in colorful graffiti and peace messages.
day_by_day.evening: Cross Charles Bridge again and head into Staré Město (Old Town). Visit the Old Town Square and watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) strike the hour — free to watch from outside. Climb the Old Town Hall Tower (~130 CZK) for panoramic sunset views over the red rooftops of Prague.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre-style budget option: grab a fresh pastry and coffee at a local pekárna near Hradčany for ~60–80 CZK.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Kampa Island — buy supplies from Albert supermarket or a local market: bread, cheese, cured meats, and Czech beer for ~100–130 CZK total.
meals.dinner: Restaurace U Parlamentu or try Maitrea (vegetarian-friendly, Old Town) — budget set lunch menus often available in the evening too. Alternatively, grab a hearty bowl of goulash at a pub near Old Town Square for ~150–200 CZK.

day_by_day.notes: September weather in Prague is mild (15–20°C) and ideal for walking. Wear comfortable shoes — Hradčany and Malá Strana involve cobblestones and inclines. Book St. Vitus Cathedral tickets online in advance to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Josefov (the Jewish Quarter) — one of Europe's best-preserved Jewish heritage sites. The combined ticket for all synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery costs ~500 CZK and is absolutely worth it. Visit the hauntingly beautiful Old Jewish Cemetery, the Pinkas Synagogue (with names of 80,000 Holocaust victims inscribed on walls), and the Spanish Synagogue with its stunning Moorish interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí) via metro — the heart of modern Prague and site of key historical events including the 1989 Velvet Revolution. Visit the National Museum at the top of the square (entry ~200 CZK, free on first Wednesday of month — check if applicable). Then explore the Vinohrady neighborhood for its Art Nouveau architecture and local café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Prague's famous classical music scene on a budget — look for student orchestra concerts or evening organ recitals in historic churches (St. Nicholas Church in Malá Strana often hosts concerts for ~350–500 CZK). Alternatively, explore the lively Žižkov neighborhood for cheap local bars and authentic nightlife away from tourist traps.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy (splurge option, ~150 CZK for coffee and pastry) OR a budget bakery near your hotel (~60 CZK).
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá in Old Town — excellent value Czech classics, lunch specials around ~150–180 CZK with a beer.
meals.dinner: Žižkov neighborhood pub crawl dinner — try Pivnice U Sadu or any local hospoda (pub) for beer and cheap Czech food. Budget ~120–160 CZK for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter is deeply moving — allow at least 3 hours and go with a respectful mindset. Audio guides are available at the ticket office. Josefov gets crowded by midday, so arriving at opening time (9:00) is strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or morning visit to Vyšehrad Fortress — take Metro Line C to Vyšehrad station. This hilltop fortress offers FREE entry to the grounds, stunning views over the Vltava River, and the Vyšehrad Cemetery where Czech luminaries like Dvořák and Smetana are buried. Walk the ramparts and explore the Romanesque rotunda. Far fewer tourists than Prague Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center and visit the Prague City Museum (Muzeum hlavního města Prahy) near Florenc — entry ~120 CZK. See the incredible 1:480 scale model of 19th-century Prague. Then stroll through Náměstí Míru square in Vinohrady and browse local shops and markets. Visit the Farmers' Market at Náměstí Míru if operating (Fridays and Saturdays).
day_by_day.evening: Last evening in Prague — revisit your favorite spot (Charles Bridge at night is magical). Enjoy a farewell Czech dinner and pack your bags for the morning journey to Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a hearty Czech breakfast at a local kavárna — eggs, cold cuts, and coffee for ~100 CZK.
meals.lunch: Street food near Vyšehrad or pack snacks from a supermarket. Try a langos (fried dough with toppings) from a street stall for ~80 CZK.
meals.dinner: Česká restaurace U Fleků — Prague's oldest brewery (est. 1499) in Nové Město. Dark beer brewed on-site, traditional Czech food. Budget ~250–300 CZK for food and drinks — a splurge but worth it as a farewell Prague experience.

day_by_day.notes: Tonight, pack and prepare for tomorrow's early journey to Budapest. Book your Budapest accommodation in advance. Check train or bus schedules: RegioJet or FlixBus Prague–Budapest runs ~6–7 hours and costs €15–30 if booked ahead — far cheaper than flying.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Prague to Budapest by overnight or morning bus/train (RegioJet recommended — comfortable, affordable, with onboard snacks). Depart ~07:00–08:00 from Praha Florenc bus station or Praha hlavní nádraží (main train station). Enjoy the Central European countryside en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Budapest Keleti or Népliget station around 13:00–14:00. Check into your Budapest budget accommodation (hostel or guesthouse in District VII — the Jewish Quarter / ruin bar district is ideal and affordable). Drop bags and head straight to the iconic Hungarian Parliament Building exterior — best viewed from across the Danube on the Buda side or from Kossuth Lajos tér. Interior tours available (~8,000 HUF / ~€20) — book online.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side as the city lights up. Cross the famous Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot for free — stunning views of Buda Castle and the Parliament. Explore the Castle District from below or take the funicular up (~1,200 HUF one way).

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks or buy from a bakery near Prague's bus station before departure. RegioJet buses often include a small snack and drink.
meals.lunch: Eat on the bus or grab a quick bite upon arrival — look for a lángos stand near Keleti station (~600–800 HUF).
meals.dinner: Welcome to Budapest! Dine at Frici Papa Kifőzdéje (District VII) — a legendary no-frills Hungarian canteen beloved by locals. Hearty goulash, stuffed cabbage, and chicken paprikash for ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~€6–9).

day_by_day.notes: Budapest is significantly cheaper than Prague — your budget will stretch further here. Download the BKK app or buy a 72-hour Budapest transport pass (~5,500 HUF) for unlimited metro, tram, and bus travel. Exchange currency at official bureaux de change — avoid airport kiosks and street exchangers.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill — take Metro M2 to Batthyány tér, then Bus 16 or the Castle Bus (Várbusz) up to the hill. Visit the Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom, entry ~2,500 HUF) with its stunning geometric tiled roof, and the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — exterior viewing is FREE, interior towers ~1,000 HUF. Panoramic views of the entire city and the Danube are spectacular. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Buda side and visit the Budapest History Museum inside Buda Castle (~2,800 HUF) — excellent exhibits on the city's Roman, medieval, and Ottoman past. Then cross back to Pest and explore the Great Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok) on Fővám tér — a stunning 19th-century iron-and-brick market. Browse paprika, salami, embroidered goods, and cheap street food on the ground floor.
day_by_day.evening: Sunday evening is perfect for Budapest's famous ruin bar scene. Head to District VII (Erzsébetváros) and visit Szimpla Kert — the original and most famous ruin bar, housed in a decaying building filled with eclectic décor, local art, and cheap craft beer (~800–1,200 HUF per pint). Sunday evenings have a farmers' market inside Szimpla (10:00–14:00 — note for future reference).

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh pastries (kifli, pogácsa) from a local pékség (bakery) near your accommodation for ~300–500 HUF.
meals.lunch: Ground floor of the Great Market Hall — try lángos with sour cream and cheese (~800–1,000 HUF), or pick up fresh produce and assemble a cheap picnic.
meals.dinner: Kádár Étkezde (District VII) — a legendary Budapest canteen open only for lunch/early dinner. Traditional Jewish-Hungarian cuisine, cash only, incredibly cheap (~2,000–3,000 HUF for a full meal). Arrive early as it fills up fast and closes by 15:30 on weekdays — on Sundays check hours, or opt for Spinoza Café nearby (~3,500–4,500 HUF).

day_by_day.notes: Fisherman's Bastion is extremely photogenic — visit early morning or late afternoon for the best light and fewer crowds. The ruin bars of District VII are a uniquely Budapest cultural phenomenon — even if you're not a big drinker, visiting Szimpla Kert for the atmosphere is a must.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dohány Street Synagogue (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and one of the most beautiful. Entry ~5,000 HUF includes access to the Hungarian Jewish Museum and the moving Holocaust Memorial Garden with its weeping willow Tree of Life sculpture. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Located in District VII, steps from the ruin bar district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) at the end of Andrássy Avenue — FREE to visit and one of Budapest's most iconic landmarks, featuring the Millennium Monument with statues of Hungarian chieftains and kings. Walk through City Park (Városliget) behind it — free and beautiful. Visit the exterior of Vajdahunyad Castle within the park (free grounds). Optionally, visit the Museum of Fine Arts on the square (~3,200 HUF).
day_by_day.evening: Splurge-worthy budget experience: visit the Széchenyi Thermal Baths (Széchenyi fürdő) in City Park — one of the largest spa complexes in Europe. Evening entry (after 18:00) is often discounted (~6,000–7,000 HUF vs. ~8,500 HUF daytime). Soaking in the outdoor pools under the stars surrounded by Neo-Baroque architecture is an unmissable Budapest experience.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty tér — a Budapest institution since 1858. Coffee and a slice of Dobos torte (~2,500–3,000 HUF) is a worthy splurge, or opt for a cheaper local café nearby (~600–800 HUF for coffee and pastry).
meals.lunch: Andrássy Avenue has several affordable lunch spots — try Hungarikum Bisztró or any étkezde (canteen) along the way for a set lunch menu (~2,500–3,500 HUF for 2 courses).
meals.dinner: After the baths, grab street food or a quick meal near Széchenyi — try a kürtőskalács (chimney cake) as a snack (~800 HUF) and a light dinner at a nearby pub for ~2,500–3,000 HUF.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a towel and flip-flops to the thermal baths (or rent them there for ~500–800 HUF each). Lockers are included in entry. The evening atmosphere at Széchenyi is magical — often less crowded than daytime. Book online in advance to secure your spot and potentially save money.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum, ~2,000 HUF) in District VIII for a comprehensive overview of Hungarian history from prehistoric times to the 20th century. Alternatively, walk up Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) — FREE — for the absolute best panoramic view of Budapest, the Danube, and both Buda and Pest. Visit the Citadella fortress at the top and the Liberty Statue (Szabadság-szobor).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the Great Market Hall (if you missed it earlier) or along Váci Street. Pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, Unicum liqueur, or embroidered folk items as gifts. Visit the Central Market or browse the flea market at Ecseri Piac if time allows (take Bus 54 from Boráros tér — ~30 min, open Mon–Fri and Sat morning).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Budapest, then transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport or your onward destination. Take the 100E Airport Express bus from Deák Ferenc tér (~900 HUF, ~30–40 min) — the most affordable airport transfer option.

meals.breakfast: One last Hungarian breakfast — rántotta (scrambled eggs) with fresh bread and coffee at a local vendéglő for ~1,200–1,500 HUF.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the city center — try a bowl of gulyásleves (goulash soup) at a local étkezde for ~1,500–2,000 HUF.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Borkonyha Winekitchen (splurge, Michelin-starred but surprisingly affordable lunch/early dinner at ~8,000–12,000 HUF per person) OR keep it budget-friendly at Menza Restaurant on Liszt Ferenc tér (~4,000–5,500 HUF) — stylish retro-socialist décor, excellent Hungarian classics.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in. Budapest Airport is about 16 km from the city center. The 100E bus is the cheapest option; taxis cost ~8,000–10,000 HUF. Double-check your flight time and terminal. Safe travels — this has been an incredible Eastern European adventure!

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Airport Express bus or taxi to your boutique hotel in Hradčany district (~45 min ride). Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with a hotel map.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle introductory stroll through Hradčany (Castle District). Walk along Hradčanské náměstí (Castle Square), admire the baroque facades, and peek at the exterior of Prague Castle without going inside yet. Wander down Nerudova Street, lined with charming Renaissance and Baroque houses, soaking in the atmosphere of your neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Malá Strana (Little Quarter), a short walk downhill from Hradčany, for your first evening in Prague. Explore the lantern-lit cobblestone streets and visit the iconic Charles Bridge at dusk for atmospheric views of the Vltava River and illuminated cityscape.

meals.breakfast: Onboard flight or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Café Savoy (Malá Strana) — elegant yet mid-range café with Czech classics like svíčková and freshly baked pastries; great for a first proper Prague meal
meals.dinner: Restaurace U Maltézských rytířů (Malá Strana) — cozy candlelit cellar restaurant serving traditional Czech cuisine (roast duck, goulash); mains ~400–600 CZK

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Buy a Prague public transport pass at the airport (3-day or 24-hour) for trams and metro. September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–20°C), perfect for evening walks. Carry some Czech Koruna (CZK) for smaller restaurants and tips.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex exploration — start early (gates open 9:00) to beat crowds. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral (stunning Gothic interior and stained glass), the Old Royal Palace (Vladislav Hall), and the Golden Lane (tiny medieval houses where Franz Kafka briefly lived). Allow 3–4 hours for the full complex. Book tickets online in advance (~350 CZK for Circuit B).
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through the castle gardens (Královská zahrada) and cross the Vltava via Charles Bridge, pausing to admire the 30 Baroque statues. Continue into Staré Město (Old Town). Visit the Old Town Square, watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime on the hour, and explore the Týn Church. Optional: climb the Old Town Hall Tower for panoramic views (~130 CZK).
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Vinohrady or Josefov (Jewish Quarter) neighborhood — stroll through the historic Jewish Quarter, view the exterior of the Old Jewish Cemetery and synagogues (open until 18:00 in September). End the evening with a beer at a traditional Czech pivnice (pub).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Eska Bakery nearby — excellent sourdough, pastries, and specialty coffee; budget ~150–200 CZK
meals.lunch: Lokál Hradčany or a picnic from a local deli near the castle — grab open-faced chlebíčky (Czech sandwiches) and eat in the castle gardens
meals.dinner: Kolkovna Olympia (Malá Strana) — popular mid-range Czech brasserie, famous for Pilsner Urquell on tap and hearty Czech dishes; mains ~300–500 CZK

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is one of the largest castle complexes in the world — wear comfortable shoes. The castle grounds are free to enter; fees apply for individual buildings. September light is beautiful for photography — golden hour hits the castle around 18:30. Book any popular restaurants in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mucha Museum (dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha) in Nové Město — a compact but rich museum perfect for 1.5 hours. Then walk to Wenceslas Square, the historic heart of Czech national identity, and explore the National Museum at its top end (recently renovated, excellent historical collections; entry ~200 CZK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to the Vinohrady neighborhood for a relaxed afternoon. Browse the Náměstí Míru square and its Neo-Gothic St. Ludmila Church. Visit the Vršovice or Žižkov districts for a taste of local, non-touristy Prague. Climb the Žižkov Television Tower (quirky Communist-era landmark with crawling baby sculptures; observation deck ~250 CZK) for the best panoramic views of Prague.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Prague — return to Old Town for a farewell dinner and a night walk across Charles Bridge (magical with fewer crowds after 21:00). Stop for a Trdelník (chimney cake) from a street vendor as a sweet send-off.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre (Nové Město) — historic Viennese-style café frequented by Kafka and Einstein; try eggs Benedict or Czech pancakes; ~200–300 CZK
meals.lunch: Manifesto Market (Vinohrady, open seasonally) — hip container food market with diverse street food options; budget ~150–250 CZK
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant (Staré Město) — upscale-casual modern Czech cuisine using seasonal ingredients; mid-range splurge night; tasting menu or à la carte ~600–900 CZK per person

day_by_day.notes: This is your last full day in Prague before moving to Budapest tomorrow. Pack your bags tonight and confirm your train/bus booking to Budapest. The RegioJet or FlixBus overnight or morning trains from Praha Hlavní nádraží to Budapest Keleti take ~7 hours. Book in advance for best prices (~€20–40).

day_by_day.morning: Morning departure from Prague to Budapest by train or bus (depart ~07:00–09:00 from Praha Hlavní nádraží). The scenic journey through Central European countryside takes approximately 6–7 hours. Pack snacks and enjoy the views — you'll pass through Slovak landscapes and the Danube valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Budapest Keleti Station (~14:00–16:00). Check into your Budapest accommodation (pre-booked mid-range hotel recommended in District V — Inner City, or District VII — Jewish Quarter, for central access). Drop bags and take a first walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side — stunning views of Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and Parliament.
day_by_day.evening: Explore District VII — the Jewish Quarter and Budapest's famous ruin bar scene. Visit Szimpla Kert, the original and most iconic ruin bar, housed in a crumbling pre-war building filled with eclectic décor, local art, and live music. Great for drinks and a unique cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab pastries and coffee at Praha Hlavní nádraží station before boarding, or enjoy café car on the RegioJet train
meals.lunch: Onboard snacks or stop at a station café during the journey
meals.dinner: Kárpátia Restaurant (District V, Budapest) — grand historic Hungarian restaurant in a stunning neo-Gothic interior; try goulash, chicken paprikash, and Hungarian wines; mains ~3,000–5,000 HUF

day_by_day.notes: Currency changes from CZK to HUF (Hungarian Forint) — exchange at the station or use an ATM in Budapest (avoid airport exchange kiosks with poor rates). Budapest is divided by the Danube: hilly Buda (castles, history) on the west and flat Pest (nightlife, culture) on the east. Get a Budapest transport card for metro, trams, and buses.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Buda Castle District — take the Funicular (Budavári Sikló) from Clark Ádám tér up to Buda Castle (~1,200 HUF return). Visit the Hungarian National Gallery inside the castle (free entry to permanent collection) and walk through the medieval Castle Quarter. Don't miss Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — seven Neo-Romanesque towers with the most photogenic views of Parliament and the Danube; free entry to terraces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) adjacent to Fisherman's Bastion — a stunning Gothic church with colorful Zsolnay tile roof; entry ~1,800 HUF. Descend to the Buda side and walk across the iconic Széchenyi Chain Bridge to Pest. Explore Lipótváros (Leopold Town) and visit the magnificent Hungarian Parliament Building exterior (one of the world's largest parliaments); book interior tours in advance (~8,000 HUF).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube — many operators offer 1-hour evening cruises (~5,000–8,000 HUF) with spectacular views of illuminated bridges, Buda Castle, and Parliament. Book at the dock near Vigadó tér. Afterward, explore the elegant Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's Champs-Élysées — lined with Neo-Renaissance mansions.

meals.breakfast: Gerbeaud Café (Vörösmarty tér) — Budapest's most famous historic café since 1858; try Gerbeaud cake (layered walnut and apricot jam) with coffee; ~2,000–3,000 HUF
meals.lunch: Hungarikum Bisztró (near Buda Castle) — casual, authentic Hungarian bistro; hearty langos (fried dough) or bean goulash; budget ~2,000–3,500 HUF
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen (District V) — Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant with creative Hungarian cuisine and excellent wine list; mid-range splurge; ~5,000–8,000 HUF per person

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means more crowds at Fisherman's Bastion — arrive before 9:30 AM for the best experience and photos. The Danube cruise is especially magical in September with clear skies and warm evenings. Wear layers as evenings can cool to 12–15°C.

day_by_day.morning: Experience a traditional Budapest thermal bath — visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath in City Park (one of Europe's largest; entry ~7,000–9,000 HUF including locker). Spend 2–3 hours soaking in the outdoor and indoor pools fed by natural hot springs. A quintessential Budapest experience, especially atmospheric on a cool September morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) surrounding Széchenyi Baths — visit the fairy-tale Vajdahunyad Castle (free exterior, small museum inside) and Heroes' Square (Hősök tere), a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring the Millennium Monument with statues of Hungarian chieftains and kings. Walk back along Andrássy Avenue and stop at the House of Terror Museum (former secret police headquarters; ~4,000 HUF) — a sobering and powerful historical experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) if still open (closes 15:00 on Sundays — adjust timing) or browse the Jewish Quarter's evening atmosphere. Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe; evening exterior is beautifully lit. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in District VII.

meals.breakfast: Street food near Széchenyi Baths — grab a lángos (fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a market stall; ~800–1,200 HUF
meals.lunch: Café Kör (District V) — beloved local bistro with daily specials; try Hungarian beef stew or stuffed cabbage; ~2,500–4,000 HUF
meals.dinner: Macesz Bistro (District VII, Jewish Quarter) — modern Jewish-Hungarian cuisine in a warm, intimate setting; try cholent or matzo ball soup; mains ~3,500–5,500 HUF

day_by_day.notes: Book Széchenyi Baths online in advance on weekends to guarantee entry and preferred cabin/locker type. Bring flip-flops and a towel (or rent on-site). The House of Terror has deeply emotional content about Nazi and Soviet-era atrocities — allow 1.5–2 hours and be prepared for a heavy but important historical experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or deeper local exploration — visit the charming Óbuda (Old Buda) district, the oldest part of Budapest with Roman ruins. See the Aquincum Museum and Roman Amphitheater (~1,500 HUF) — remnants of a major Roman city. Alternatively, take a 45-minute HÉV suburban train to Szentendre, a picturesque Danube Bend artists' village with Serbian Orthodox churches, folk art museums, and cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: If in Szentendre: explore the Open-Air Ethnographic Museum (Skanzen — one of Europe's largest folk museums; ~2,500 HUF) and browse local galleries and marzipan shops. Return to Budapest by 16:00. If staying in Budapest: visit the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum, District VIII; ~2,000 HUF) — comprehensive history of Hungary from prehistoric times to the present, housed in a grand Neo-Classical building.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Budapest — splurge on a cultural experience. Attend an opera or concert at the Hungarian State Opera House (Magyar Állami Operaház) on Andrássy Avenue — one of the world's most beautiful opera houses; tickets from ~3,000–15,000 HUF depending on seat. Alternatively, enjoy a classical concert at the Liszt Ferenc Academy of Music (~3,000–6,000 HUF).

meals.breakfast: Auguszt Cukrászda (historic pastry shop) — try rétes (strudel) and coffee; ~1,000–1,500 HUF
meals.lunch: In Szentendre: Rab Ráby Restaurant — Hungarian classics in a historic cellar; OR in Budapest: Menza (Liszt Ferenc tér) — retro-socialist design with modern Hungarian comfort food; ~2,500–4,000 HUF
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown (District V) — Budapest's acclaimed fine dining with Hungarian ingredients; pre-opera dinner; mid-range splurge ~8,000–12,000 HUF per person; OR Spinoza Café (Jewish Quarter) — cozy café-restaurant with live klezmer music some evenings; ~3,000–5,000 HUF

day_by_day.notes: Book opera tickets well in advance — September is peak cultural season and performances sell out. The State Opera House also offers guided tours (~3,000 HUF) if evening shows are sold out. The Szentendre day trip is highly recommended for a change of pace from city exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — revisit any missed highlights or do some last-minute souvenir shopping at the Great Market Hall (opens 06:00 Mon–Fri, 08:00 Sat; closed Sunday). Pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, Unicum herbal liqueur, and hand-embroidered folk textiles. Take a final walk across the Liberty Bridge (Szabadság híd) — one of Budapest's most elegant bridges — for a last Danube view.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure preparation — check out of accommodation and head to Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport (BUD) by taxi or the 100E airport bus from Deák Ferenc tér (~900 HUF, ~30–40 min). Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for international flights. Reflect on an incredible 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's greatest cities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight from Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerloczy (District V) — charming Art Nouveau café near Ferenciek tere; full Hungarian breakfast with eggs, cold cuts, and coffee; ~2,000–3,000 HUF
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the Great Market Hall food stalls (upper floor) — try lángos, stuffed cabbage, or goulash soup before heading to the airport; ~1,500–2,500 HUF
meals.dinner: Airport dining or onboard flight

day_by_day.notes: Keep some HUF for the airport bus and last-minute purchases. The 100E airport bus is the most economical option (~900 HUF vs ~8,000–12,000 HUF for taxi). Double-check flight departure terminal. Consider downloading offline maps of both cities (Maps.me or Google Maps offline) before the trip. September is an ideal travel month — fewer crowds than summer, pleasant temperatures, and vibrant cultural calendars in both Prague and Budapest.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 – no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Václav Havel Airport to your boutique hotel in Hradčany district. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your elegant surroundings with views of Prague Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: After freshening up, take a leisurely guided walk through the Hradčany Castle Quarter – the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Explore the outer courtyards, admire St. Vitus Cathedral's Gothic façade, and stroll along Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička), the charming row of colorful 16th-century artisan cottages. Enjoy the sweeping panoramic views over the red-roofed city below.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a prestigious restaurant in the Hradčany or Malá Strana area. Consider Field Restaurant or Alcron for an exceptional Czech fine-dining experience. After dinner, take a magical evening stroll across the illuminated Charles Bridge – far fewer crowds at night, with lantern light reflecting on the Vltava River.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable – arrival day
meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at the hotel or a nearby café such as Café Savoy for elegant Czech pastries and coffee
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant (Michelin-starred, modern Czech cuisine) – tasting menu with wine pairing recommended

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with your hotel concierge. Request early check-in if possible. Keep the afternoon pace relaxed to recover from travel. Hradčany is walkable from the hotel – no transport needed.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a full immersive tour of Prague Castle complex. Visit the interior of St. Vitus Cathedral including the Royal Crypt and Crown Jewels chamber (advance tickets recommended). Explore the Old Royal Palace and St. George's Basilica with a private guide for deeper historical context on Bohemian kings and Holy Roman Emperors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) via Nerudova Street, lined with Baroque palaces and noble residences. Visit the ornate Church of St. Nicholas. Cross Charles Bridge in daylight to admire its 30 Baroque statues. Enter Staré Město (Old Town) and explore the Old Town Square, including the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the Gothic Týn Church.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private classical music concert – Prague is renowned for intimate chamber concerts held in Baroque palaces and churches. The Lobkowicz Palace concerts or Municipal House events are world-class. Afterward, enjoy a nightcap at the rooftop bar of a luxury hotel such as the Mandarin Oriental Prague.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel – request a full Czech breakfast with cold cuts, local cheeses, fresh bread, and coffee
meals.lunch: Café Louvre or Grand Café Orient in Old Town – elegant Art Nouveau interiors with Czech and European cuisine
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise – Michelin-starred, celebrating historic Czech recipes with a modern tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague Castle timed entry tickets in advance online. Hire a private guide for the castle (2–3 hours) for a richer experience. Wear comfortable walking shoes – cobblestones throughout. September weather is typically mild and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) – one of the best-preserved Jewish historic districts in Europe. Tour the six historic synagogues (Old-New Synagogue, Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting Holocaust memorial, Spanish Synagogue with stunning Moorish interiors) and the medieval Old Jewish Cemetery. A private guide brings centuries of history vividly to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vltava riverbanks with a private luxury boat cruise along the river, gliding past Charles Bridge, Prague Castle, and the city's elegant waterfront. Alternatively, visit the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha, then browse the upscale boutiques of Pařížská Street (Prague's answer to the Champs-Élysées) for luxury shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the stunning Estates Theatre (Stavovské divadlo) – where Mozart personally premiered Don Giovanni in 1787. This is one of Europe's most historically significant opera houses. Book premium seats well in advance.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with fresh fruit, yogurt, and Czech pastries
meals.lunch: Kolkovna Celnice – upscale Czech brasserie near the Jewish Quarter, excellent svíčková (beef sirloin) and Czech pilsner
meals.dinner: Pre-theatre dinner at V Zátiší – refined Czech and international cuisine in an intimate setting near the Estates Theatre

day_by_day.notes: Jewish Quarter entry requires a combined ticket – purchase in advance. Estates Theatre tickets sell out quickly; book at least 2–3 weeks ahead. The boat cruise can be arranged through the hotel concierge as a private charter.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Český Krumlov or Kutná Hora – two of Bohemia's most spectacular UNESCO World Heritage sites. Recommended: Kutná Hora (1.5 hours from Prague by private car). Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) – decorated with the bones of 40,000 people – and the magnificent Gothic Cathedral of St. Barbara, a masterpiece rivaling Prague's St. Vitus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kutná Hora's medieval silver-mining heritage at the Czech Museum of Silver, including a guided underground mine tour. Stroll through the beautifully preserved historic town center. Return to Prague by private car in the late afternoon, arriving refreshed for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Prague – your last evening in the city. Choose a table at Eska (creative modern Czech) or return to a favorite from earlier in the trip. After dinner, take one final atmospheric walk across Charles Bridge and through the Old Town, savoring the illuminated city before tomorrow's departure.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Dacický – a historic restaurant in a medieval building, serving traditional Bohemian cuisine with local wines
meals.dinner: Eska Restaurant – acclaimed farm-to-table Czech cuisine in a beautifully converted industrial space in Prague's Žižkov district

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver for the Kutná Hora day trip (round trip ~3 hours driving total). The Bone Church has timed entry – book online. Pack a light jacket as underground mine tours can be cool. This is your last night in Prague – pack and prepare for Budapest departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to Prague Main Station or airport for travel to Budapest. The scenic Railjet train (Praha–Budapest, ~6.5 hours) is a premium experience with comfortable first-class seats and beautiful Central European countryside views. Alternatively, a short flight (~1.5 hours) for maximum efficiency. Depart mid-morning to arrive in Budapest early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest and check into your luxury accommodation (recommend Four Seasons Gresham Palace or Aria Hotel Budapest). After settling in, take an introductory walk along the Danube embankment – a UNESCO World Heritage site. Admire the iconic Hungarian Parliament Building from across the river and stroll along the elegant Chain Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner in Budapest at Costes Downtown or Onyx Restaurant – both Michelin-starred and celebrating Hungarian gastronomy at its finest. After dinner, take a night cruise on the Danube for breathtaking illuminated views of the Parliament, Castle Hill, and the bridges. Budapest is arguably even more spectacular at night.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at your Prague boutique hotel before departure
meals.lunch: First-class dining car on the train, or a packed gourmet picnic prepared by the hotel; alternatively airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown – Michelin-starred Hungarian fine dining with exceptional wine pairing from the Tokaj region

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets (first class) or flights well in advance. The Four Seasons Gresham Palace is one of Europe's most iconic Art Nouveau hotels, located directly at Chain Bridge – request a Danube-view room. The evening Danube cruise can be arranged as a private luxury boat charter through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Chain Bridge to Buda side and ascend Castle Hill by funicular (Budavári Sikló) for panoramic views. Explore the Royal Palace (Buda Castle) complex housing the Hungarian National Gallery with masterworks of Hungarian fine art. Visit Matthias Church – one of Hungary's most ornate Gothic churches with stunning Zsolnay ceramic roof tiles – and the Fisherman's Bastion with its fairy-tale Neo-Romanesque towers and unrivaled views over Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Buda waterfront and cross back to Pest. Visit the magnificent Hungarian Parliament Building on a guided VIP interior tour – the largest parliament building in Europe, adorned with gold leaf, frescoes, and housing the Hungarian Holy Crown. Then explore the elegant Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées, UNESCO-listed) toward Heroes' Square and the Millennium Underground (Europe's second-oldest metro).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House – one of the most beautiful opera houses in the world, with a gilded Neo-Renaissance interior. Pre-book premium box seats. Enjoy a post-opera drink at the New York Café – the world's most beautiful café, a gilded Belle Époque masterpiece.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast at the Four Seasons or Aria Hotel
meals.lunch: Halászbástya Restaurant at Fisherman's Bastion – panoramic terrace dining with traditional Hungarian goulash and fish dishes
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Borkonyha Winekitchen (Michelin-starred) – Hungarian seasonal cuisine with outstanding local wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours require advance booking – VIP tours offer smaller groups and additional access. Opera tickets must be booked weeks in advance for premium seats. The New York Café is open late and ideal for a nightcap – try their famous Esterházy cake.

day_by_day.morning: Experience Budapest's legendary thermal spa culture – a cornerstone of Hungarian identity. Visit the Széchenyi Thermal Baths (largest in Europe) or the more intimate and architecturally stunning Gellért Baths for a private VIP spa session. Enjoy thermal pools, steam rooms, and optional massage treatments. This is a deeply restorative and culturally authentic Budapest experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Jewish Quarter and the magnificent Dohány Street Synagogue – the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world, with a stunning Byzantine-Moorish interior. Visit the adjacent Jewish Museum and the moving Holocaust Memorial Garden (the Weeping Willow sculpture). Then browse the Great Market Hall (Vásárcsarnok) for luxury Hungarian artisan goods – Tokaji wine, Herend porcelain, paprika, and embroidery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube – arrange a private luxury boat with champagne and canapés as the golden hour light bathes the Parliament and Castle Hill. This is one of the most spectacular views in all of Europe. Afterward, dine at Gerbeaud Salon or 21 Magyar Vendéglő for a refined final evening in Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square – Budapest's most historic and elegant café, founded 1858; excellent Hungarian cakes, coffee, and light lunches
meals.dinner: 21 Magyar Vendéglő – sophisticated modern Hungarian cuisine in a stunning historic setting near the Opera House

day_by_day.notes: Book the Gellért or Széchenyi spa in advance and request a private cabin for changing. Herend porcelain (available at the Great Market Hall or dedicated boutiques) makes an exceptional luxury souvenir. The private sunset cruise should be arranged through the hotel concierge – specify champagne service and a bilingual guide.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest – visit the Museum of Fine Arts at Heroes' Square (one of Central Europe's great art museums, housing works by Raphael, El Greco, Goya, and Rembrandt) or the Hungarian National Museum for a deep dive into 1,000 years of Hungarian history. Alternatively, take a peaceful walk through Városliget (City Park) and admire the Vajdahunyad Castle – a romantic replica of Transylvanian architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping along Váci Street or the designer boutiques of Andrássy Avenue. Visit a Herend or Zsolnay porcelain boutique for premium Hungarian artisan pieces. Enjoy a final coffee and cake at a historic Budapest café. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure – carry the memories of two of Central Europe's most magnificent capitals: the golden spires of Prague and the grand boulevards of Budapest.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final hotel breakfast – request the full spread including Hungarian specialties such as lángos, túrós táska, and local honey
meals.lunch: Spoon The Boat – elegant floating restaurant on the Danube with panoramic views, serving refined European cuisine; perfect farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining – request special meals in advance if flying business or first class

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for the airport transfer and check-in. Store luggage at the hotel after checkout for a hassle-free final morning. Consider arranging a private city highlights drive-by on the way to the airport for one last look at the Parliament and Chain Bridge. Confirm all departure logistics with the hotel concierge the evening before.
